problem: Find the value of $c$ that satisfies the mean value theorem for integrals for $f(x)=3{x}^{2}-2$ on the interval $[1,3].$

feedback.problem: Find the value of $c$ that satisfies the mean value theorem for integrals for $f(x)=2x$ on the interval $[-1,4].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for the integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4-(-1)}{\int }_{-1}^{4}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{5}\cdot ({x}^{2})|}_{-1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[{4}^{2}-(-1)^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(16-1) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =3 \\ 2c & =3 \\ c & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
